question.problem:
Consider the following data sets:

$$
x = \big\{ 13, \: 10, \: 9, \: 12 \big\},\qquad
y = \big\{ -1, \: 3, \: 2, \: 4 \big\}
$$

You are given that $\overline{x}=11$ and $\overline{y}=2.$ Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
The linear correlation coefficient $\rho$ of the data sets $x=\big\{ x_1,x_2, \ldots, x_n \big\}$ and $y=\big\{ y_1,y_2, \ldots, y_n \big\}$ is given by 

$$
\rho(x,y) =  \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}(x,y)}{\sigma_x \cdot \sigma_y} = \dfrac{S_{xy}}{\sqrt{S_{xx} \cdot S_{yy}}}.
$$

First, we compute the sum in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =(13-11)(-1-2)+(10-11)(3-2) \\  & +(9-11)(2-2)+(12-11)(4-2) \\  & =(2)(-3)+(-1)(1)+(-2)(0)+(1)(2) \\  & =-6-1+0+2 \\  & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we compute the sums in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =(13-11)^{2}+(10-11)^{2}+(9-11)^{2}+(12-11)^{2} \\  & =4+1+4+1 \\  & =10 \\ {S}_{yy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2} \\  & =(-1-2)^{2}+(3-2)^{2}+(2-2)^{2}+(4-2)^{2} \\  & =9+1+0+4 \\  & =14\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho (x,y) & =\frac{(-5)}{\sqrt{10}\cdot \sqrt{14}} \\  & ≈-\frac{5}{3.162\,278\cdot 3.741\,657} \\  & ≈-0.42\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
